title: High-Speed DI with Approximation
tagline: Year 4 — Estimating growth, shares and ratios from large tables in seconds by rounding to two figures

introduction.overview: In a timed DI section you cannot afford exact division on every question. When the options are well separated, rounding the data to two significant figures gives an answer accurate enough to pick the right one. The method is to round, compute with easy numbers, and compare with the options; when two options lie within 2–3% of each other, switch to exact calculation for that question only.
introduction.placementRelevance: Speed in DI decides how many sets you finish; approximation is the main speed tool.
introduction.realWorldContext: Managers estimate growth and shares in meetings without a calculator.

learningObjectives: Judge the precision from the option spacing
Switch to exact calculation when options are close

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Growth ≈ change ÷ old. Round numerator and denominator in a way that keeps the ratio close.

coreDefinitions: Error budget: how much error you can afford.
Exact switch: calculating precisely when needed.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: If the options are 8% apart, a 2% error cannot change your answer.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Round, estimate, compare with the options; refine only if two options are close.

mainNarrative: Company A grew from 3,420 to 4,260: the change is 840, about 24.6% of 3,420; estimate 840 ÷ 3,400 ≈ 25%.
Company C grew from 2,760 to 3,540: change 780; 780 ÷ 2,760 = 28.3%; estimate 780 ÷ 2,800 ≈ 28%.
Total revenue in 2023 is 4,260 + 5,870 + 3,540 + 4,380 + 2,610 = 20,660; a rounded sum gives about 20,700.
Revenue per employee of company B is 5,870 ÷ 940 ≈ 6.2 crore.
If the options were 24%, 25% and 26%, you would calculate exactly.

deepDiveAspects.title: Round in the same direction for a ratio
deepDiveAspects.content: Rounding numerator and denominator both up cancels part of the error.

solvedExamples.title: Growth
solvedExamples.question: Company A rose from 3,420 to 4,260. Estimate the growth.

solvedExamples.title: Per head
solvedExamples.question: B has revenue 5,870 and 940 employees. Estimate revenue per employee.

solvedExamples.title: Exact switch
solvedExamples.question: Options are 24%, 25% and 26%. What should you do?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Round to two figures, estimate, compare; switch to exact only if options are within 2–3%.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Reject options far from the estimate.
